newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees unified security depositary system.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees unified security depositary system.

text.p: Russia's leading securities depositary and clearing bodies said on Monday they would soon sign an agreement to work towards a unified depositary system, which they say is needed to boost Russia's emerging markets.
Plans for a unified system have been held up for months by a row between the central bank and a key securities regulator over control of Russia's equity and government securities markets.
But First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said at the end of last month agreement had been reached on a single regulatory system for both markets.

The National Depositary Centre (NDC) and the Depositary Clearing Company (DCC) said on Monday they would now not wait for a government resolution on depositary activity being prepared by a working group from the central bank, Federal Commission for the Securities Market and the Finance Ministry.
But they would consult with all three.
"We need to receive support from all three organs," said Igor Moryakov, first deputy president of DCC.
"Their latest joint actions indicate that the matter has at last moved out of stalemate and is moving toward the formation of a single market system."
But they said they would be guided by market needs, rather than bureaucratic manoeuvring in working on the standards.
The agreement, to be approved within days, calls for unified standards to be brought into force by October 1, 1997, and for a unified electronic accounting system by November 1.
Despite rapid development over the past few years, Russia's emerging securities markets are still hobbled by clumsy and inadequate infrastructure.
The formation of the Depositary Clearing Company by leading brokerages in 1994 demolished one of the major obstacles facing early investors in Russia's fledgling market.

But some market players say Russia needs a unified system for depositing and clearing both corporate and government paper, and needs to do away with the time- and money-consuming process of re-registering shares after sales.
"This is the main thing braking the development of the market," said Moryakov.
But forming a truly unified depositary system will take time, NDC director Galina Starodubtseva said, adding the agreement was open to other depositary organisations.
A recent government decree ordered domestic and foreign shareholders in natural gas producer Gazprom to re-register their shares with another organisation, the Depositary Clearing Union.
